headline: Global Emissions Drop for Fourth Consecutive Month
meta_description: Global greenhouse gas emissions fell 0.1% in May 2026 compared to last year, marking four months of decline or plateau.
summary_short: For the fourth month running, global greenhouse gas emissions have plateaued or declined, with May 2026 showing a 0.1% drop year-over-year.
body:
Global greenhouse gas emissions have plateaued or fallen for four consecutive months, with May 2026 marking a 0.1% decline compared to May 2025. The shift reflects progress across major emitting nations.

China led the reductions, decreasing emissions by 8.5 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent year over year. Russia also contributed to the global downward trend, further supporting the consecutive months of stalled or falling emissions.

While a single month's data point remains modest, four months of sustained decline or plateau suggests a potential turning point in global efforts to slow atmospheric carbon accumulation. The pattern indicates that combined actions across different regions may be beginning to reshape emission trajectories at scale.
quick_facts: Fourth consecutive month of plateau or decline
China cut 8.5 million tonnes CO2 equivalent year-over-year
Russia also reduced emissions in the same period
